response.sql:
WITH linked_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    o.orderbase,
    f.feerate
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fees f ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
),
channel_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    orderbase,
    AVG(feerate) as avg_rate
  FROM linked_fees
  GROUP BY orderbase
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(feerate) as bench_rate
  FROM linked_fees
),
above_bench AS (
  SELECT 
    ca.avg_rate,
    (ca.avg_rate - b.bench_rate) as excess
  FROM channel_avg ca
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE ca.avg_rate > b.bench_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_rate) as mean_of_avg_rates,
  AVG(excess) as mean_of_exceedance
FROM above_bench;

alternatives.interpretation: The benchmark could be the mean of channel averages (equal weight per channel) rather than the mean of all fee records (equal weight per fee), if 'average fee rate over all those linked fee records' is interpreted as averaging the pre-computed channel means.
